changelog: Two changes in one update. The System Health screen's network check now reports two separate things: whether the Ethernet port has a connection, and whether this system can actually reach the internet -- including which connection is carrying the traffic when it is not the cable. And the system now checks its own update source at every start and at every update check: if it was ever left pointing somewhere other than the official release -- which silently freezes a system on its old version -- it corrects itself and carries on updating.
details: v50 is the combined fleet release of two bench revisions -- 50a (internet reachability on the System Health network row) and 50b (the manifest self-heal, v13's rescue repair made permanent on the main line) -- and it widens the payload to the full 24-file ship set. Reachability (50a): v48b's network row could report the Ethernet port's link only, so a unit whose cable was unplugged -- or whose port was dead, the customer case behind v48b -- showed a warning and nothing else while the system was in fact still online. cytech_check_eth.sh now makes a second, independent measurement: an outbound TCP connect() probe to well-known public anycast endpoints (1.1.1.1:443, 8.8.8.8:53, 9.9.9.9:443, 223.5.5.5:443, first answer wins), addressed by IP only so a DNS failure can never read as 'no internet'. The probe runs twice: first source-bound to the port's own IPv4, where success means the port's address carried the traffic (net='port'); if that fails, once unbound, where success means the system is online through some other connection (net='other'), and net_via names the interface the successful connect() actually left from -- wl* rendered as 'Wi-Fi', usb*/enx* as 'a USB network adapter'. Neither succeeds -> net='none'. The result file gains net, net_via and net_message; sensor.cytech_ethernet_result exposes net and net_message as attributes under the SAME unique_id (no new entity) and dashboards/system.yaml renders one badge per fact. The port line keeps its OK and NO_IFACE wording, but its NO_LINK text drops the 'online via X' sentence, which the internet line now says more accurately (a link is not reachability); a port with a link and no reachability now names the problem as further along the network, which is the distinction this change exists for. Still display-only: no email, no popup, no alert kind. Offline-test-only env overrides (CY_ETH_DEV, CY_ETH_CARRIER, CY_ETH_IP, CY_NET_TARGETS) make every branch reproducible without unplugging anything, all strictly read-only. Self-heal (50b): a unit whose CYTECH_MANIFEST_URL is not the canonical main one cannot update at all, and neither failure looks like a failure. The retired test branch leaves it on whatever version that branch serves, reporting 'up to date' -- truthfully, relative to that frozen source -- forever; any other ref (a release tag left behind by a service visit, a commit SHA, or no ref at all) makes cytech_update.sh build a download base that 404s, so the owner sees 'Update failed while downloading <file>. Will retry on next boot.', which never resolves. The repair -- already published to the frozen class on the test branch as v13 -- now lives in first_boot.sh and cytech_check_only.sh on main, so it reaches every unit that ever gets these scripts, including ones sealed in their box, since the boot call sits above the .zero_touch_completed branch and runs before anything reads the URL. Scope is deliberately narrow: it rewrites the URL only when the host is raw.githubusercontent.com, the repo path is exactly slychiu/ComfortHA-yaml, and the ref is something other than main (test, a tag, a SHA, or missing). A local test mirror, another repo, a nested path, a foreign host or a non-manifest path is left strictly alone -- verified by the unit suite, which also covers the surrounding shapes, a quoted value, a trailing CR, a commented-out line, an already-correct file (silent no-op, no backup) and a missing file (fresh unit, no crash). The original value is kept once in /config/.cytech_secrets.bak_pre_manifest_repair and never overwritten; a unit that already carries the v13 rescue's backup keeps it and this line writes its own. The in-process variable is refreshed, so the very press that repairs the URL already checks against the real latest instead of waiting for the next pass. The widened payload: this release's files list is the full 24-file ship set rather than just the changed files, because an update replaces only the files a release lists and nothing else ever syncs a unit's file set -- so a unit that reached the current version by jumping over releases (the v12/v13 rescue path), or was flashed from an SD image older than a release that first delivered a file, is missing files no later release would ever send it. The consequences were concrete and all owner-visible: enable_remote_support.sh exits 1 without operator_pubkey.txt, so the Remote Support toggle flips on and installs no key; the v49 package calls cytech_alert_mail.py, which only v48 ever delivered, so alert mail fails (rc 127) on any unit that skipped v48; first_boot.sh's ensure_yaml_dashboards() registers all five YAML dashboards unconditionally and strips the storage-mode registry entries, so a unit missing the four dashboard files would replace working sidebar pages with dead entries; and cytech_integrity_check.py is what the 4-hourly self-check and the System Health buttons run. Shipping the full set costs one larger download and converges every unit's file set onto the fleet's current one whatever its history; the two retired storage-mode dashboard payloads (welcome_dashboard.json, zones_dashboard.json) stay out, as ever. Of the 24 files, 17 are byte-identical to the copies v48 shipped; 7 changed (first_boot.sh, cytech_check_only.sh, cytech_check_eth.sh, packages/cytech.yaml, dashboards/system.yaml, enable_remote_support.sh, disable_remote_support.sh) and cytech_update.sh is re-shipped unchanged, which also converges rescue-healed units onto the current updater (the v11-era one has no tag-scoped downloads and no Core-restart triggers). Verification: 50a was bench-verified 2026-09-22 on cytech.local from the served bytes -- the check offered it, all three files landed md5-identical to the tag blobs, Core restarted (packages changed), the boot automation ran the new script and wrote the new result schema, the shipped dashboard YAML rendered both badges and rendered an old-schema result file without a stray badge, and all seven status/reachability branches were exercised live through the read-only overrides (0-6 s each) alongside 13 unit tests on the shipped python. 50b was bench-verified the same day: both repair paths exercised live -- boot path (URL pinned to /48/manifest.json, restart, boot pass repointed it to main, logged the repair, wrote its own backup, left the version and every other secrets line untouched, offered no spurious update) and Check path (URL set to the retired test branch; that single press both repaired the URL and reported 'System is up to date'), with the narrow scope confirmed on the bench as well (a local test-mirror URL produced no repair line and no backup), plus a 98-assertion unit suite against the function text extracted from the two committed scripts, passing on the PC and on the bench against the deployed copies. The rescue flow these repairs serve has since been confirmed on real customer hardware: a unit frozen at v11 reached the current release unaided, its owner pressing only Check for Update and Update Now.
